choices.outcome: Best answer. Regulators expect honest, complete information. Showing known weaknesses with a credible fix, while protecting personal information, is far stronger than a clean-looking but incomplete file.

choices.text: Backfill missing complaint entries from memory so the register looks complete.
choices.outcome: This creates false records, which is a serious honesty problem for the bank and for the people involved, and would make matters far worse if discovered.

choices.text: Send only Pieter's competence records and say the complaints data is not ready.
choices.outcome: Partly honest, but it leaves the request unanswered and gives no plan. The regulator will see a gap without an explanation.

choices.text: Delay until the investigation closes so there is nothing open to mention.
choices.outcome: Stalling a regulator's request is poor conduct and could be seen as uncooperative. Deadlines can be discussed openly, not simply ignored.

cards.title: Amanzi Bank's conduct and competence programme

items.label: Board and senior management
items.detail: Set a fair-treatment culture and oversee conduct risk.

items.label: Key individuals
items.detail: Manage and oversee financial services; approved by the FSCA.

items.label: Compliance and learning teams
items.detail: Policies, competence register, CPD plans, monitoring, reporting.

items.label: Branch and team leaders
items.detail: Supervise representatives and act on gaps and red flags.

items.label: Every representative
items.detail: Stay fit and proper, disclose, treat customers fairly, speak up.

cards.caption: The roles are Amanzi Bank's. The duties behind them come from BN 194 of 2017, the Conduct Standard for Banks as the FSCA describes it, the Protected Disclosures Act and POPIA.

cards.title: Handle a protected disclosure well
cards.prompt: Put the bank's steps in a sensible order.
steps: Receive the disclosure through the authorised internal procedure
Protect the discloser's identity and any personal information involved
Within 21 days, decide whether to investigate or refer, and inform the discloser in writing
Investigate and keep the discloser updated if the decision takes longer
Fix the wrongdoing, including customer redress where needed
Tell the discloser the outcome and record lessons for training

cards.question: Which of these is the bank's own duty under section 6(2) of the Protected Disclosures Act?
options: Pay every whistle-blower a reward
Report every disclosure to the FSCA within a week
Authorise internal procedures and make all staff aware of them
Keep disclosures out of any investigation
cards.explanation: Section 6(2)(a) requires every employer to authorise appropriate internal procedures for receiving and dealing with information about improprieties and to take reasonable steps to bring them to the attention of every employee and worker.

cards.title: Real case: what the FSCA said it would watch (2025)
cards.body:
The FSCA closed its 2025 banking complaints review with clear next steps. It said it would keep monitoring how banks address the shortcomings and implement its recommendations, aiming for:

- **standardised procedures**
- **proper employee training**
- **continuous monitoring** by the banks themselves
- **changes made** when and where needed

Those four points are a useful checklist for assessment readiness in any conduct area. When the regulator asks for evidence, a bank should be able to show the procedure, who was trained on it and when, how it monitors its own performance, and what it changed after finding a problem.

cards.title: Getting ready for the final exam
cards.body:
Before you start the final boss:

- **Fit and proper:** the six requirements, ongoing compliance and the duty to disclose.
- **Competence:** experience, qualifications, RE 5 and RE 1, class and product training before rendering services, Tier 1 versus Tier 2.
- **CPD:** the 1 June to 31 May cycle, 6/12/18 hours, accreditation, deadlines of 15 and 30 days, five-year records.
- **TCF and complaints:** the six outcomes, African Bank's advert, the 2025 review findings.
- **Speak up and confidentiality:** the PDA's protections and 21-day response, POPIA's confidentiality duties.

cards.title: Stage five take-aways
items: Every employer must authorise internal procedures for disclosures of wrongdoing and make all employees and workers aware of them.
A protected disclosure may not lead to occupational detriment such as dismissal, demotion, harassment or an unwanted transfer.
Disclosures under the internal route need a written decision within 21 days; knowingly false, harmful disclosures are an offence.
POPIA requires confidentiality, security safeguards and prompt notification of compromises to the Information Regulator and customers.
Assessment readiness means honest records, trained people, self-monitoring and visible fixes.

cards.prompt: If you saw a colleague mis-selling tomorrow, do you know exactly where your bank's speak-up procedure is and who would receive your report? If not, find out today.

quiz.question: Under the Protected Disclosures Act, which of these can be the subject of a disclosure?
options: A disagreement about office seating
A failure to comply with a legal obligation
A colleague's choice of holiday
A dislike of a new product's colour
quiz.explanation: The Act's definition covers information showing, for example, a criminal offence, a failure to comply with a legal obligation, danger to health or safety, environmental damage, unfair discrimination or concealment of these.

quiz.question: Which of these is listed as an occupational detriment in the Protected Disclosures Act?
options: Being refused a promotion because of a disclosure
Receiving routine training on new products
Being thanked publicly for raising concerns
Being asked for evidence during an investigation
quiz.explanation: Being refused transfer or promotion is one of the listed detriments, along with dismissal, suspension, demotion, harassment, unwanted transfer and adverse references.

quiz.question: A disclosure is made through Amanzi Bank's internal procedure and the discloser is known. Within how many days must the bank decide whether to investigate or refer it and inform the discloser in writing?
options: 7 days
30 days
21 days
90 days
quiz.explanation: Section 3B requires the recipient to decide and inform the employee or worker in writing as soon as reasonably possible, and in any event within 21 days.

quiz.question: Amanzi Bank's employment contract says staff 'must never raise concerns about the bank outside their reporting line'. Under the Protected Disclosures Act, what is the effect of that clause?
options: It is fully binding on all employees
It applies only to contractors
It is valid if staff signed it
It is void to the extent it discourages protected disclosures
quiz.explanation: Section 2(3) makes void any contract provision that tries to exclude the Act or that has the effect of preventing or discouraging a protected disclosure.

quiz.question: An employee knowingly reports false allegations about a colleague, intending to harm him, and he suffers harm. What does the Protected Disclosures Act provide?
options: It is still a protected disclosure
It is a criminal offence
It only affects the colleague's rights
It must be ignored by the employer
quiz.explanation: Section 9B makes it an offence to intentionally disclose information known, or reasonably known, to be false, with intent to cause harm, where harm results.

quiz.question: Under POPIA, how must a person processing customer information on the bank's behalf treat it?
options: As public once it is in the bank's systems
As shareable with any colleague who asks
As confidential, disclosing only as law or proper duties need
As confidential only after the account closes
quiz.explanation: Section 20 requires anyone processing personal information on behalf of a responsible party to act only with its authorisation and treat the information as confidential, disclosing it only if required by law or for proper performance of duties.

quiz.question: A branch laptop holding customer records is stolen. Under POPIA, what must the bank do when there are reasonable grounds to believe the information was accessed or acquired?
options: Notify the Information Regulator and affected customers as soon as reasonably possible
Notify only the police and wait for an arrest
Notify customers only if they ask
Wait 90 days to see if any data is misused
quiz.explanation: Section 22 requires notification to the Regulator and the data subjects as soon as reasonably possible after discovery, allowing for law enforcement needs and steps to establish the scope.

quiz.question: Which statement about the bank's speak-up duties under the Protected Disclosures Act is correct?
options: Only permanent employees may be protected
Only managers may receive disclosures
Only disclosures to the media are protected
Workers such as contractors and agents are also covered
quiz.explanation: Since the 2017 amendments the Act covers workers, including independent contractors, consultants and agents, and the employer must bring its procedures to the attention of every employee and worker.

quiz.question: The FSCA asks for evidence and the complaints register has gaps. Which response best reflects good assessment readiness?
options: Disclose the gaps honestly with a dated remediation plan
Fill the gaps from memory before sending
Send nothing until all gaps are closed
Send only the strongest records
quiz.explanation: Regulators expect accurate and complete information. Showing known gaps with a credible plan is honest and constructive; recreating records or withholding them raises serious integrity concerns.

quiz.question: Which set matches the next steps the FSCA said it would monitor after its 2025 banking complaints review?
options: Higher fees, faster closures, fewer ombud cases
New branches, more staff, larger budgets
Standardised procedures, proper training, self-monitoring and change
Shorter letters, fewer records, automated rejections
quiz.explanation: The FSCA said it would monitor banks to ensure standardised procedures, proper employee training, continuous monitoring by the banks themselves and implementation of changes where necessary.

references.title: Determination of Fit and Proper Requirements for Financial Services Providers, 2017 (Board Notice 194 of 2017)
references.issuer: FSCA (formerly Registrar of Financial Services Providers)
references.note: Six fit and proper requirements applying continuously; duty to disclose; general competence and FSP controls; RE before appointment; class and product training before rendering services; competence register; CPD cycle, hours, deadlines and reductions; Tier 1 and Tier 2 products.

references.title: Banking Sector Complaints Management Review Report (February 2025)
references.provision: Review of section 8 of Conduct Standard 3 of 2020 (Banks)
references.note: Desktop review of 23 banks' complaints handling; findings on categorisation, recording, data, acknowledgement, keeping complainants informed and ombud details; good practices, recommendations and next steps including proper employee training.

references.title: FSCA Press Release: FSCA publishes complaints management review report on the banking sector (17 March 2025)
references.note: States that Conduct Standard 3 of 2020 (Banks) became effective in July 2021 and summarises the review's key challenges.

references.title: FSCA Press Release: FSCA imposes administrative penalty on African Bank Limited for misleading advertising (22 April 2025)
references.provision: Conduct Standard 3 of 2020, sections 6(1), 6(3)(a)-(b) and 6(9), as described by the FSCA
references.note: R700 000 penalty (R200 000 suspended) for a loan advert presented as an investment and weak advert approval governance.

references.title: FSCA study on financial customer behaviour and sentiment (TCF outcomes)
references.note: Describes the six Treating Customers Fairly outcomes, introduced under the FSB in 2011, and the FSCA's mandate under section 57 of the FSR Act.

references.title: Protected Disclosures Act 26 of 2000 (as amended by Act 5 of 2017)
references.issuer: Parliament (Department of Justice and Constitutional Development)
references.note: Employers must authorise internal procedures and make every employee and worker aware of them; no occupational detriment for protected disclosures; written response within 21 days; knowingly false harmful disclosures are an offence.

references.title: Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013
references.issuer: Parliament (Department of Justice and Constitutional Development)
references.note: Security safeguards, confidentiality for those processing on the bank's behalf, operator notification, notification of compromises to the Regulator and data subjects, and the information officer's role.

references.title: FSCA Press Release: The FSCA urges financial institutions to verify validity of CPD providers (19 June 2025)
references.note: Warning about LearnOn issuing CPD certificates without authorisation; institutions should verify CPD providers with professional bodies.

references.title: FSCA Press Release: warning against individuals selling fraudulent Regulatory Examination (RE) certificates (18 December 2023)
references.note: Forged RE certificates sold on social media; candidates and employers told to deal with and verify through the approved examination body.

references.title: FSCA Press Release: FSCA imposes debarment orders on Mr Eric Anthony Wood and Mr Niven Magandheran Pillay (14 August 2026)
references.note: 18-year debarments for conduct inconsistent with honesty and integrity at the Regiments FSPs.

references.title: FSCA Press Release: The FSCA imposes an administrative penalty and debarment on Mr Jacobus Stephanus Geldenhuis (18 December 2023)
references.note: 20-year debarment and about R143 million penalty for unauthorised financial services (FAIS s 7(1)) and conducting the business of a bank.

references.title: FSCA Press Release: The FSCA makes a debarment order in respect of Mr Craig Roy Warriner (21 May 2024)
references.note: 30-year debarment for acting as an unauthorised discretionary FSP; public urged to check the category of advice an adviser is authorised for.

bank.question: Amanzi Bank's call-centre agent explains the interest rate and notice period of a 32-day deposit, then says, 'Given your plans, this one is right for you.' How should the bank classify the second statement?
options: As factual information, which any trained agent may give
As an intermediary service needing no appointment
As advice, which only an appointed representative may give
As marketing, which falls outside FAIS entirely
bank.explanation: Telling a customer which product suits his plans is a recommendation based on his circumstances, which is advice. Quoting the rate and notice period alone would be factual information.

bank.question: Which statement best describes how long the FAIS fit and proper requirements apply to a representative?
options: They apply before appointment and continuously while appointed
They apply only during the first year of appointment
They apply only when a new product is launched
They apply only until the regulatory exam is passed
bank.explanation: The Determination requires a person to comply to be appointed and, to remain appointed, to comply at all times with the applicable requirements.

bank.question: A key individual at Amanzi Bank discovers that another key individual no longer meets a requirement of the Determination. What does BN 194 of 2017 require of the FSP?
options: Wait for the next annual review
Record it and act within one CPD cycle
Tell the board at its next meeting only
Notify the regulator immediately
bank.explanation: Section 13(7) requires an FSP to notify the regulator immediately after it becomes aware, or has information reasonably suggesting, that a key individual does not or no longer complies with the Determination.

bank.question: Which pair of fit and proper requirements in BN 194 of 2017 relate mainly to the FSP as a business rather than to each individual's character or knowledge?
options: Honesty and good standing
Operational ability and financial soundness
Competence and CPD
Integrity and product training
bank.explanation: Operational ability (people, systems, governance) and financial soundness concern the FSP's capacity as a business. The others relate to the person's character and knowledge.

bank.question: A candidate disclosed that, eight years ago, a professional body reprimanded her for a minor administrative lapse unrelated to honesty. How should the bank approach this under BN 194 of 2017?
options: Reject her automatically for any past reprimand
Ignore it because it is older than five years
Weigh its seriousness, relevance to the role and the time since
Ask the FSCA to decide her appointment for it
bank.explanation: Section 9(3) requires due regard to seriousness, relevance to the duties and the passage of time. There is no automatic bar, and no fixed cut-off that makes old events irrelevant.

bank.question: Which of these events in a candidate's history is listed in BN 194 of 2017 as indicating a possible lack of honesty, integrity or good standing?
options: Providing false information to a regulator
Changing employers twice in five years
Failing a university module once
Taking extended parental leave
bank.explanation: Being knowingly untruthful or providing false or misleading information to, or being uncooperative with, the regulator is one of the listed incidents in section 9.

bank.question: In the FSCA's 2023 Geldenhuis matter, what made his activity unlawful under FAIS from the outset?
options: He failed to complete his CPD hours for that cycle
He advised on Tier 2 products without RE 5
He kept advice records for less than five years
He was neither an authorised FSP nor a representative of one
bank.explanation: The FSCA found that neither he nor his company was an authorised FSP or representative, contravening section 7(1) of the FAIS Act, and that he ran a Ponzi-type scheme. He was debarred for 20 years.

bank.question: What does the FSCA's 2026 Wood and Pillay debarment show about the honesty and integrity requirement?
options: It only applies to people currently employed by banks
Past conduct can still lead to long debarments years later
It can be met by passing an ethics exam
It lapses once a firm's licence lapses
bank.explanation: The FSCA debarred both men for 18 years in 2026 for conduct between 2009 and 2016, showing that honesty and integrity concerns can be acted on long after the events and after licences lapse.

bank.question: A representative at Amanzi Bank receives a summons in a civil fraud claim. She tells nobody, reasoning that she has not been found liable. Which duty has she most likely breached?
options: The duty to complete class of business training
The duty to submit CPD evidence within 15 days
The duty to disclose relevant information to the FSP promptly
The duty to keep a competence register
bank.explanation: Section 10 requires a representative to disclose to its FSP, promptly, fully and on her own initiative, any information that may be relevant to her honesty, integrity and good standing, not only final findings.

bank.question: Amanzi Bank appoints a consultant to advise only on ordinary short-term and long-term deposits. Which combination of requirements applies to her under BN 194 of 2017?
options: Product specific training, but no RE, class training or CPD
RE 5, class training and product training, but no CPD
CPD only, because deposits are simple products
No competence requirements, as deposits are excluded
bank.explanation: Representatives who only render services on Tier 2 products are excluded from the regulatory exam, class of business training and CPD requirements, but product specific training still applies.

bank.question: Why is a deposit whose return depends on a share index treated differently from an ordinary fixed deposit under BN 194 of 2017?
options: It is a long-term deposit, which is a Tier 2 product
It is a structured deposit, which is a Tier 1 product
It is not a financial product under FAIS at all
It is an insurance product under the Short-term Act
bank.explanation: A deposit whose return or value depends on an underlying product, asset, rate or index is a structured deposit, listed as Tier 1. Ordinary short-term and long-term deposits are Tier 2.

bank.question: Amanzi Bank plans to let a new hire advise on a structured deposit from day one and train her in her first month. What is wrong with this plan?
options: Structured deposits need no product training
Training must wait until after the CPD cycle
Only key individuals need product training
Training must be completed before rendering services
bank.explanation: Section 29(1) requires the class of business and product specific training relevant to the product to be completed before rendering any financial service on it.

bank.question: Which of these topics is listed for product specific training rather than class of business training in BN 194 of 2017?
options: The range of products within the whole class
General role players in the class of business
The lock-in periods, exit options and their costs
The impact of economic cycles on the class
bank.explanation: Product specific training covers matters such as lock-in periods, termination conditions, exit options and associated costs. The other topics are listed for class of business training.

bank.question: Which regulatory examination does Table A of BN 194 of 2017 require of representatives, where the examination requirement applies?
options: RE 5
RE 1
RE 3
RE 4
bank.explanation: Table A lists RE 5 for representatives in every category. Key individuals and FSPs write RE 1, with RE 3 or RE 4 added for some categories.

bank.question: A bank uses telephone staff to execute scripted sales of a Tier 1 product without giving advice. Which control is among the conditions in BN 194 of 2017 for relaxing the qualification requirement for such staff?
options: Staff hold a postgraduate qualification
Calls are recorded, stored and retrievable
Sales are approved by the FSCA in advance
Customers sign a waiver of advice rights
bank.explanation: The conditions include a Grade 12 or equivalent, an approved script, direct oversight by a key individual, recorded and retrievable calls, and controls to prevent advice and unfair sales practices.

bank.question: How long must the FSP retain records of a representative's product specific training under BN 194 of 2017?
options: At least one year after the training date
Until the end of the next CPD cycle
Only while she remains employed by the FSP
At least five years after she stops rendering services on that product
bank.explanation: Section 30(b) requires the FSP to keep training information for at least five years after the representative ceases to render services on that product or class of business.

bank.question: Pieter is asked to confirm to a product supplier that Amanzi Bank's representatives have completed the required training for its product. What does BN 194 of 2017 say?
options: The FSP may refuse, as training records are private
Only the FSCA may confirm training to suppliers
The FSP must provide confirmation within a reasonable time
Each representative must confirm it personally
bank.explanation: Section 30(c) requires the FSP to give a product supplier confirmation of the required class of business and product specific training within a reasonable time, where the supplier needs it for its own compliance.

bank.question: In its December 2023 warning about forged regulatory examination certificates, what did the FSCA invite employers to do?
options: Verify certificates directly with the examination body
Accept certificates bearing the FSCA logo
Re-test all staff with an internal exam
Report every new hire to the police
bank.explanation: The FSCA told candidates to deal directly with the approved examination body and invited employers to verify the authenticity of RE certificates with that body.

bank.question: A representative appointed for one subclass of business within one class joins on 1 March. How many CPD hours, at minimum, must she complete by 31 May?
options: 1.5 hours
3 hours
6 hours
0 hours
bank.explanation: The annual minimum for one subclass is 6 hours. Pro-rated for three months (March to May): 6 ÷ 12 × 3 = 1.5 hours.

bank.question: A consultant has twelve recorded hours from an accredited provider, plus a completed module of her degree. How do the degree module hours count towards CPD?
options: They count double because degrees are harder
They count if the university is accredited
They do not count; activity towards a qualification is excluded
They count only in her first cycle at the bank
bank.explanation: The definition of a CPD activity excludes activities performed towards a qualification and product specific training.

bank.question: Which three features must an activity have to qualify as a CPD activity under BN 194 of 2017?
options: Approved by the FSCA, free of charge and online
Accredited by a professional body, given an hour value and verifiable
Delivered in person, examined and certified
Chosen by the employee, logged and signed off
bank.explanation: A CPD activity must be accredited by a professional body, allocated an hour value by it, and be verifiable, with evidence of who took part and that they completed it.

bank.question: The CPD cycle ends on 31 May. By when must Amanzi Bank record its representatives' CPD activities in the competence register?
options: Within 15 days after the cycle ends
Within 90 days after the cycle ends
By the end of the next cycle
Within 30 days after the cycle ends
bank.explanation: Section 32(3)(a) requires the FSP to record the CPD activities within 30 days after each cycle expires. Representatives must submit their evidence within 15 days.

bank.question: A representative's absence for caring for her child with a long-term illness begins in one cycle and continues without a break. What is the maximum period over which the bank may reduce her CPD hours?
options: Three consecutive CPD cycles
One CPD cycle only
Two consecutive CPD cycles
Five consecutive CPD cycles
bank.explanation: Reductions for qualifying absences may run into consecutive cycles only where the absence continues uninterrupted, and then for a maximum of three consecutive cycles.

bank.question: A team leader asks to reduce a representative's CPD hours because she was 'too busy with targets' this year. What should Pieter answer?
options: Yes, if her targets were exceeded
Yes, but only by half the hours
Workload is not a ground for reduction
Yes, if the team leader signs it off
bank.explanation: Section 34 allows pro rata reductions only for continuous absence due to parental or adoption leave, long-term illness or disability, or caring for a family member with a long-term illness or disability.

bank.question: Which item must an FSP's CPD policies and procedures include under section 32(2) of BN 194 of 2017?
options: A list of approved restaurants for workshops
Training plans for each CPD cycle
A bonus scheme linked to CPD hours
A ban on online CPD activities
bank.explanation: The FSP's CPD policies must include how people will maintain, update and develop their knowledge and skills, and training plans for each cycle that address gaps and improve professional standards.

bank.question: In its 2025 LearnOn warning, what risk did the FSCA say institutions faced if they failed to verify CPD providers?
options: They might lose their banking licence immediately
They might owe the provider extra fees
They might have to repeat regulatory exams
They might not meet their BN 194 CPD requirements
bank.explanation: The FSCA warned that failing to verify CPD providers and programmes may result in institutions not meeting their CPD requirements under BN 194 of 2017.

bank.question: Amanzi Bank's competence reviews look only at whether staff passed their exams. Which element does section 13(4) of BN 194 of 2017 require the reviews to consider as well?
options: Changes in products, markets and legislation
Staff members' social media activity
The bank's share price performance
Customers' personal credit records
bank.explanation: Section 13(4) requires evaluations to consider technical knowledge and its application, skills and expertise, and changes in the market, financial products and services, and legislation.

bank.question: Amanzi Bank designs a high-fee investment account and markets it heavily to low-income pensioners who need easy access to cash. Which TCF outcome is most directly breached?
options: A fair culture built into leadership
Products designed to meet the needs of the targeted customers
Suitable advice where advice is given
No unreasonable post-sale barriers
bank.explanation: Outcome 2 expects products to meet the needs of the customer groups they target, and to be marketed and distributed accordingly. Here the product and the target market do not fit.

bank.question: A customer wants to move her savings to another bank, but Amanzi Bank requires her to visit a branch in person three times and charges an unexplained exit fee. Which TCF outcome is most at risk?
options: Products are designed for the target market
Advice is suitable for the customer
A fair culture is built into the bank
Customers face no unreasonable post-sale barriers
bank.explanation: Outcome 6 expects customers to be able to change products, switch, claim, complain or exit without unreasonable barriers.

bank.question: In the African Bank case, what besides the advert's content did the FSCA find deficient?
options: The governance and approval of the advert
The bank's complaints categorisation
The bank's CPD records for advisers
The bank's capital adequacy ratios
bank.explanation: The FSCA also found deficiencies in the governance and oversight processes for reviewing and approving the advert, contravening section 6(9) of the Conduct Standard.

bank.question: Why did the FSCA regard presenting a personal loan as 'an investment' as harmful to customers?
options: It overstated the bank's capital strength
It breached the bank's sponsorship contract
It hid the longer-term risks and costs of credit
It used a language other than English
bank.explanation: The FSCA said positioning the product as an investment rather than credit misled customers about, among other things, the longer-term risks and potential costs of taking it up.

bank.question: How many complaints did the 23 banks' registers contain for the period covered by the FSCA's 2025 banking complaints review?
options: About 31 600
About 316 000
About 3.1 million
About 23 000
bank.explanation: The registers held 316 133 complaints for July 2021 to June 2022. The FSCA sampled up to 100 complaints per bank.

bank.question: Amanzi Bank's complaints register shows each complaint as 'resolved' or 'pending' only. Which weakness from the FSCA's 2025 review does this repeat?
options: Failure to give the handler's contact details
Failure to categorise complaints at closure
Too many separate complaints systems
No indication whether complaints were upheld or rejected
bank.explanation: The FSCA found registers showed status as resolved or pending without saying whether the complaint was upheld or rejected, weakening oversight of complaints data.

bank.question: Which of these did the FSCA record as good practice after its banking complaints review?
options: Automatic escalation to management when a service level is breached
Closing complaints automatically after 30 days
Referring card fraud complaints to the police only
Recording goodwill payments only in monthly slides
bank.explanation: One major bank built automatic escalation into its system when the service level agreement is breached. Recording goodwill only in presentations was a weakness the FSCA criticised.

bank.question: Sipho finds that complaint data on the register does not match customer details in the core banking system. What did the FSCA recommend?
options: Delete the register and rely on the core system
Ask customers to resubmit their complaints
Align customer details on the register with the bank's systems
Stop recording customer details on complaints
bank.explanation: One recommendation was to ensure alignment between customer details captured on complaints registers and those captured on the bank's systems.

bank.question: The FSCA found that 92% of banks fell short on a section 8 requirement. Which one?
options: Keeping complainants informed of progress, delays and decisions
Categorising complaints in the minimum categories
Maintaining complaints data by category
Securely recording complaints information
bank.explanation: 92% of banks did not keep complainants adequately informed. Categorisation failures affected 60%, data maintenance 70% and secure recording 85%.

bank.question: Lerato reports wrongdoing through Amanzi Bank's speak-up procedure. The bank cannot decide within 21 days whether to investigate. What does the Protected Disclosures Act require?
options: Nothing until the decision is made, however long
Tell her in writing and update her at intervals of no more than two months
Close the matter after 21 days with no action
Refer it to the FSCA without telling her
bank.explanation: Section 3B(3) requires the recipient to inform the discloser in writing that it cannot decide within 21 days, update her at least every two months, and decide within six months.

bank.question: A dismissal because an employee made a protected disclosure is treated under the Labour Relations Act as what?
options: A fair dismissal for operational reasons
A dismissal for misconduct
A matter only for civil courts
An automatically unfair dismissal
bank.explanation: Section 4(2)(a) of the Protected Disclosures Act deems a dismissal in breach of section 3 to be automatically unfair for Labour Relations Act purposes.

bank.question: Amanzi Bank uses a contractor to run its call centre. A contractor agent reports mis-selling through the bank's procedure. Is the agent covered by the Protected Disclosures Act?
options: No, only the bank's permanent employees are covered
Only if the agent has worked there for a year
Yes, workers such as contractors and agents are covered
Only if the disclosure is made to the media
bank.explanation: Since 2017 the Act protects workers, including independent contractors, consultants and agents, and the employer must make every employee and worker aware of its procedures.

bank.question: An employee who believes she may be victimised after a protected disclosure asks to move to another division. What does the Act provide?
options: She must be transferred if reasonably possible, on terms no less favourable
She must resign and reapply for the new post
She may move only at a lower salary
She must wait until the investigation ends
bank.explanation: Section 4(3) and (4) give her the right, if reasonably possible, to a transfer, and her terms may not be less favourable without her written consent.

bank.question: Which of these is part of a responsible party's security duty under section 19 of POPIA?
options: Publish all safeguards on the bank's website
Ask customers to design the bank's safeguards
Review safeguards only after a breach
Regularly verify that safeguards are effectively implemented
bank.explanation: Section 19(2) requires the bank to identify foreseeable risks, maintain safeguards, regularly verify that they work, and keep them updated for new risks.

bank.question: An outsourced card processor suspects someone accessed Amanzi Bank's customer data without authority. Under POPIA, what must the processor do?
options: Notify only the affected customers
Notify the bank immediately
Wait for the bank's annual audit
Delete the data and say nothing
bank.explanation: Section 21(2) requires an operator to notify the responsible party immediately where there are reasonable grounds to believe personal information was accessed or acquired by an unauthorised person.

bank.question: The FSCA asks for evidence of representatives' competence. Which record should Amanzi Bank be able to produce as its central source?
options: The staff canteen roster
The branch sales leaderboard
The competence register
The marketing campaign calendar
bank.explanation: Section 13(5) requires the FSP to keep a competence register recording qualifications, regulatory exams, class and product training and CPD for itself, its key individuals and representatives.

bank.question: Which approach best shows a bank is ready for a conduct review of complaints handling, in line with the FSCA's 2025 next steps?
options: A polished presentation prepared by marketing
A one-off training session after the letter arrives
A promise to update the register next year
Standard procedures, trained staff, own monitoring and recorded fixes
bank.explanation: The FSCA said it would monitor for standardised procedures, proper employee training, continuous monitoring by banks themselves and changes where needed. Evidence of all four shows readiness.
